INITIAL TOWER TECHNICAL ASSESSMENT

Project Valkyrie: EMEA Datacenter Exit & Hybrid Cloud Transformation

AETHELGARD LIFE SCIENCES

Document ID: ITTA-ALS-2026-V1.4

Date Prepared: June 4, 2026

Prepared By: Enterprise Architecture Review Board (EARB)

Target Audience:

CIO, Global IT Steering Committee,

Transformation PMO

Classification: CONFIDENTIAL - INTERNAL ONLY

1. Executive Summary

Aethelgard Life Sciences is embarking on Project Valkyrie, a strategic initiative to exit the primary EMEA datacenters located in Basel (Switzerland) and Frankfurt (Germany). This initiative is driven by impending hardware end-of-life (EOL) cycles across the legacy footprint, rigid capacity constraints limiting R&D High-Performance Computing (HPC) capabil

ending hardware end-of-life (EOL) cycles across the legacy footprint, rigid capacity constraints limiting R&D High-Performance Computing (HPC) capabilities, and absolute deadlines imposed by facility lease expirations in Q4 2027.

The Initial Tower Technical Assessment (ITTA) evaluates the current state of Aethelgard's infrastructure, network, security, and application landscapes. The target state vision encompasses a hybrid architecture, heavily leveraging Amazon Web Services (AWS) as the primary cloud service provider for modernized and re-platformed workloads. This will be seamlessly integrated with an Equinix colocation model engineered to support latency-sensitive Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES) and legacy AS/400 systems that cannot be safely refactored within the strict 18-mont

o support latency-sensitive Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES) and legacy AS/400 systems that cannot be safely refactored within the strict 18-month timeline.

This document outlines the high-level technical assessment across nine critical IT towers. It details operational dependencies, stringent GxP compliance requirements (including FDA 21 CFR Part 11), and tower-specific modernization recommendations to ensure uninterrupted operational continuity, robust security posture, and regulatory adherence throughout the transition.

2. Business Context

2.1 Demand Overview

Following the strategic acquisition of BioGenix Innovations in 2025, Aethelgard's IT footprint expanded significantly, inheriting technical debt and disparate legacy environments. The combined enterprise now supports over

helgard's IT footprint expanded significantly, inheriting technical debt and disparate legacy environments. The combined enterprise now supports over 42,000 employees globally. The Basel and Frankfurt datacenters currently host approximately 60% of Aethelgard's core commercial, clinical, and ERP workloads. The combined physical estate encompasses over 1,400 virtual machines (VMs), 6 PB of active storage, and 650 distinct business applications spanning manufacturing, HR, finance, and specialized clinical trials.

2.2 Objectives

· Infrastructure Agility: Shift from a static, CAPEX-heavy data center model to a highly scalable OPEX cloud model, specifically enabling dynamic scaling for genomics sequencing and R&D data pipelines.

· Risk Mitigation: Vacate the Basel and Frankfurt facilities pr

specifically enabling dynamic scaling for genomics sequencing and R&D data pipelines.

· Risk Mitigation: Vacate the Basel and Frankfurt facilities prior to the November 2027 lease termination to avoid multi-million-euro penalty clauses.

· Modernization: Retire 15% of the legacy application portfolio, re-platform 45% utilizing PaaS services (e.g., AWS RDS, Amazon EKS), and rehost the remaining 40% (IaaS) utilizing block-level replication.

· Regulatory Compliance: Maintain uninterrupted adherence to EMA guidelines, FDA 21 CFR Part 11, HIPAA, and GDPR regulations throughout the entire migration lifecycle.
